en: The Sūtra on the Five Divine Messengers Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Song Dynasty śramaṇa Huìjiǎn.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park. The Buddha...
He addressed the bhikṣus:
“Listen well! Take this to heart.”

With my divine eye, I clearly perceive the births and deaths of sentient beings and the paths they follow—good or evil; whether some are ugly or others are courageous and strong, whether some are timid and weak, and whether they are born into good realms or evil realms.
All that people do, they distinguish and know.

If a person acts wickedly with the body, speaks wickedly with the mouth, and thinks wickedly with the mind—slandering the worthy and the holy, seeing the heterodox as heterodox—that person, at the end of their life, will fall into the evil paths and enter hell.

If a person physically performs good deeds, speaks good words, and maintains good thoughts, praising the noble and holy ones, seeing correctly and acting correctly, then at the end of their life, they will be reborn in the heavens or among humans.
In this way, bhikṣus!
With my divine eye, I see people passing away and being reborn in the heavens or among humans.
Thus it is, bhikṣus!

With my divine eye, I observe the rain falling from the heavens into the water, seeing one bubble arise and another bubble perish; likewise, I see that when a person dies, their consciousness is reborn—some with beautiful forms and some with ugly forms, some courageous and strong and others timid and weak; some are born in happy realms and some in realms of suffering;
being born and dying of their own accord is no different from the bubbles in water.

Furthermore, it is like a person who strings lapis lazuli beads with threads of five colors; because the beads are pure, the colors of the threads—blue, yellow, red, white, and black—all appear clearly and distinctly.
My vision of the soul departing at death and being reborn is likewise.

Furthermore, it is like hanging a bright moon-jewel at the palace gate during the dark night; if someone stands on one side and observes those entering and exiting through the gate, they see each and every one of them clearly.

Furthermore, it is like standing atop a high tower and looking down at people below—those going and those coming, those running and those walking, those sitting and those standing—and seeing as people die, their spirits emerge; whether they are handsome or ugly, brave or timid, one discerns them all according to their past deeds.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:

"When a person lives in this world and is unfilial toward their parents, disrespectful toward śramaṇas and practitioners of the Way, fails to practice benevolence and righteousness, lacks a mind for cultivation, does not study the sūtras and precepts, and fears not the afterlife—when such a person dies, their soul shall fall into the realm of King Yama."
The wardens of hell then took him away and reported his transgressions to the King, saying:

"This man has acted contrary to the Dharma; he was unfilial toward his parents, disrespectful toward śramaṇas and practitioners, and did not follow benevolence and righteousness. He had no sense of conscience, possessed no merit, and felt no dread of death; he must now face the consequences.
May Your Majesty alone determine his punishment."
"In this way, King Yama, always acting with calm composure, manifests the five divine messengers through words of loyalty and righteousness, and asks:

'Did you not originally see that when people of the world were first infants, they lay stiffly upon their excrement and urine, unable to protect themselves; their mouths did not know how to speak, nor did they know the difference between good and evil?'"
The people said, "We have seen them; they all possess these [marks].
The king said:
"Do you alone not think so? Spirits follow one's conduct;

at the end of life, one will surely undergo rebirth. Although this has not yet been seen, one should always practice goodness, rectifying one's body, rectifying one's speech, and rectifying one's mind. How can you allow your heart to run wild and indulge your will?"
The man said, "It is truly because I am ignorant and dark-witted that I do not know.
The king said:
"You have committed evil through your own ignorance; it is not the fault of your parents, teachers, rulers, devas, śramaṇas, or practitioners.
The sin belongs solely to you—how can you cease [from it] merely because you find it unpleasant?"
"Now I shall accept it.
This is the first divine messenger manifested by King Yama.
King Yama asked again:
"When you were a human being, when celestial messengers arrived one after another, were you able to perceive them?
The person replied,
"Indeed, I was not aware of it."
The king said:
"Do you not see the men and women of the world who, when they grow old, have white hair and fallen teeth, become emaciated and hunched over, and must rely on a staff to rise and move about?"
The people said, "There is. The King asked:
"Do you think that you alone can escape old age?

For all people who are born, it is the nature of things that they shall grow old; while you are still in the prime of youth, you should always do good, rectify your body, speech, and mind, and practice the sutras and precepts. How can you allow yourself such self-indulgence?"
The people said,
"It is simply because they are ignorant and deluded. The king said:
"You have committed evil through your own ignorance; it is not the fault of your parents, your sovereign, the devas, śramaṇas, or practitioners of the Way.
The transgression rests solely with you—how can you cease [from it] merely because you find it unpleasant?"
"Now you shall receive [the consequences].
This is the true teaching of King Yama as it appears to the second divine messenger.
King Yama asked again:

"When you were a human being, did you not see men, women, and wives in the world who were afflicted by illness—their bodies racked with pain, unable to sit or rise in peace, their lives drawing near in anxiety and haste, and whom no physicians could treat further?"
The people said,
"There is such a thing. The king said:
"Do you think it is possible to remain free from illness?

Once a person has grown old, the law of nature dictates that they shall all fall ill. While your body is still strong and healthy, you ought to strive to do good, observing the sutras and precepts, and rectifying your body, speech, and mind. Why do you allow yourself such self-indulgence?"
The people said,
"It is simply because of ignorance and delusion. The king said:

"You have committed evil through your own ignorance; it is not the fault of your parents, your sovereign, the devas, śramaṇas, or practitioners of the Way. The transgression rests solely with you—how can you stop simply because you find it unpleasant?"
"Now I shall receive it.
This is the third divine messenger manifested by King Yama’s true teaching.
King Yama asked again:

"When you were a human being, did you not see those who die in this world? Some have their corpses buried, while others are discarded and left to decay; within one day up to seven days, the flesh and muscles rot away, and foxes, wildcats, and hundreds of birds all come to feed upon them. Is it not the case that once a person has died, their body becomes foul and putrid?"
The people said, "There is. The King said:
"Do you think you alone can attain immortality?

For all people who are born, the law of nature dictates that they must die. While in this world, you should always do good, restraining your body, speech, and mind to practice the sutras and precepts; how can you allow yourself such self-indulgence?"
People said, "It is simply because of ignorance and darkness. The King said:
"You have committed these evils yourself; it is not the fault of your parents, your sovereign, the heavens, śramaṇas, or practitioners of the Way.
The transgression is entirely yours; you cannot cease from it simply because you find it unpleasant, for now you must undergo its consequences."
"This is the fourth divine messenger manifested by King Yama’s true teaching. King Yama asked again:

"When you were a human being, did you not see those wicked people and evil sons of the world who were captured by officials and subjected to punishments according to their crimes? Did you not see them having their hands and feet severed, or their noses and ears cut off; their skin and flesh flayed, scraped, and carved; their bodies doused with hot sand and boiling grease; wrapped in fire-wreaths, hung up, or scorched by the sun; or butchered and dismembered, with poison and pain all at once?"
The people replied,
"There is such a thing. The king said:
"Do you think that evil alone can lead to liberation?

You see with your own eyes that the distinction between sin and merit in this world is clear; why do you not uphold what is good and discipline your body, speech, and mind to practice the Way according to the sutras?"
"What is it that brings one such joy?
The man replied,
"It is simply because of ignorance and delusion."
The King said:
"You have acted for yourself, committing acts of disloyalty and injustice; this is not the fault of your parents, your sovereign, the heavens, the śramaṇas, or the practitioners of the Way.
Now, these calamities and sins must be borne by you alone; how can they be halted simply because you find them unpleasant?"
“This is the fifth divine messenger appearing through the righteous teaching of King Yama.
When the Buddha had finished speaking, all the disciples received his instruction and admonition, and each came forward to pay their respects.
The Sūtra on the Five Divine Messengers Spoken by the Buddha to King Yama.
